claims: Episode 4 of 7 in 'how to become a 10X AI native developer' series
Agent fixes errors and bugs while the creator sleeps; focus shifts to product work
Agent must reproduce the error in its own cloud environment before attempting a fix
Fix is verified against the actual production data used to reproduce the bug, plus the verification skills
Risk gate: small one-off fix merges automatically; larger architectural change requests human review
Code written by Grok 4.7 is reviewed by both GPT 6.1 and Opus 5.5; merges only when all three agree it's safe
Paying for three AI subscriptions is 'not cheap' but cheaper than hiring an engineer
Yorby makes 'a decent chunk of revenue'; not perfect, makes occasional mistakes
how_to_steps: Set up an error-capture service in the app (creator uses PostHog)
Route each captured error to a bot that triggers a cloud coding agent (Cursor)
Agent step 1: reproduce the original error in its own environment; only proceed if reproducible
Agent step 2: create a fix; verify with the same production data and with the app-specific verification skills
Agent step 3: classify merge risk -- small fix merges alone; large architectural change requests review from the founder
Agent step 4: independent review by two other models (GPT 6.1 + Opus 5.5); merge only on unanimous approval
Next episode: keeping AI-written code quality high and un-bloated

relevance.why: This is the exact pattern a time-poor solo founder wants: autonomous bug-fix loop with reproduce-first, skill-based verification, risk-tiered merging and cross-model review. Transferable to Claude Code cloud sessions + GitHub Actions instead of Cursor.

implement_score.why: Doable in stages: (1) PostHog/Sentry webhook -> create GitHub issue; (2) Claude Code remote session or Action picks up issue, must reproduce via a test before fixing; (3) require verification skill pass + a second-model review; (4) auto-merge only for small diffs. Needs real investment (a day or two) and ongoing API cost; start with review-required, not auto-merge.
